timeline_text: put the date at 2029
definition_note: human-level AI
notes: also: timeline. Op-ed by Kurzweil in TIME, "Don't Fear Artificial Intelligence". Coded post_agi because the essay is about managing risk; source_type blog used for a signed opinion piece (no op-ed type in the codebook).

quote: I've stuck with my 2029 prediction, which is now a median view and there is a growing group of people who think I am too conservative.
claim_summary: Kurzweil keeps his 2029 date for human-level machine intelligence, says it is now a median view, and notes many think it too conservative.
timeline_text: I've stuck with my 2029 prediction ... a growing group of people who think I am too conservative
definition_note: human-level intelligence in a machine
notes: Kurzweil's foreword to Martine Rothblatt's book Virtually Human; the Kurzweil Library dates it 1 March 2016. The book itself may have been published earlier (2014, not checked).

quote: One is 2029, which is when computers will pass a valid Turing test, meaning they'll be indistinguishable from human intelligence in a conversation.

timeline_text: One is 2029
definition_note: 2029 = valid Turing test pass (indistinguishable from human intelligence in conversation); the same answer explains 2045, the Singularity, as when nonbiological intelligence is a billion times all human intelligence
notes: Playboy interview published 19 April 2016, reprinted in the Kurzweil Library.

quote: 2029 is the consistent date I have predicted for when an AI will pass a valid Turing test and therefore achieve human levels of intelligence. I have set the date 2045 for the 'Singularity' which is when we will multiply our effective intelligence a billion fold by merging with the intelligence we have created.
claim_summary: Kurzweil restates 2029 for a valid Turing test pass and human-level intelligence, and 2045 for the Singularity.
timeline_text: 2029 is the consistent date I have predicted
definition_note: 2029 = valid Turing test pass, which he equates with human levels of intelligence; 2045 = Singularity, multiplying effective intelligence a billion-fold by merging with AI
notes: Statement made "in a communication to Futurism" around SXSW 2017. The Kurzweil Library dates the Futurism story March 2017; the Futurism page shows only 'Updated Oct 16, 2017'.

quote: By 2029, computers will have human-level intelligence.
claim_summary: On stage at SXSW 2017, Kurzweil says computers will have human-level intelligence by 2029.
definition_note: human-level intelligence
notes: secondhand; Fox News (16 March 2017) reporting Kurzweil's SXSW session in Austin (interviewers Shira Lazar and Amy Kurzweil). Futurism carries the same quote. No recording or transcript of the session was found; a web search for it could not be run because the search budget ran out.

quote: I think we will actually beat 2029
claim_summary: Speaking to Singularity University alumni, Kurzweil says AGI will probably arrive before his 2029 date.
timeline_text: I think we will actually beat 2029

notes: secondhand; Ash Jafari's Substack post (7 July 2022) quoting Kurzweil's remarks to a Singularity University alumni reunion, video 'Ray Kurzweil - Singularity University GSP09 Metaverse Reunion April 16, 2022' (youtube.com/watch?v=5iFSz1orGUg); no transcript of the video could be read. The post also paraphrases him as saying large language model progress surprised him and no big breakthroughs are needed for AGI. A revision toward an earlier date.

quote: I'm still saying 2029, and it turns out to be pessimistic. A lot of people are saying [we will pass the Turing test] by next year.
claim_summary: Kurzweil keeps 2029 for passing the Turing test but says it now looks pessimistic, as many expect it within a year.
timeline_text: I'm still saying 2029, and it turns out to be pessimistic
definition_note: Turing test pass
notes: Bessemer Venture Partners interview (Talia Goldberg and Bhavik Nagda), published as an edited transcript 11 March 2024; the bracketed words are the publisher's. Same interview: 'I think we have the calculations. We don't have the data.' Hedge toward an earlier date.

quote: We're not quite there, but we will be there, and by 2029 it will match any person.
claim_summary: On Joe Rogan's podcast Kurzweil says AI is not yet at human level but will match any person by 2029.
timeline_text: We're not quite there, but we will be there
definition_note: match any person
notes: secondhand; also: capability_now. Business Today (13 March 2024) reporting Joe Rogan Experience episode 2117. archive.org copies of the episode have no transcript or captions; no published transcript found. Episode aired 2024-03-12 (TVmaze listing). The Independent (via Yahoo, 13 March 2024) reports a second remark from the same episode: "I'm actually considered conservative. People think that it will happen next year or the year after." A further search for a transcript (search log) found none.

quote: Well, most people now are saying it's going to happen earlier. Elon Musk says we'll do it within two years. So I'm saying five years.
claim_summary: Asked if his 2029 Turing test date still stands, Kurzweil keeps it at five years away while noting most people now expect it sooner.
timeline_text: So I'm saying five years
definition_note: AI passing the Turing test (host's question); same interview: 'I'm sticking with that prediction' for the Singularity in 2045
notes: computed: 2024 + 5. Science Friday radio interview, published transcript, 14 June 2024. Host asked whether the 2029 Turing test prediction 'still stand[s], or might it be even earlier'.

quote: I have not revised and not redefined my prediction of AGI, still defined as AI that can perform any cognitive task an educated human can. I still still believe that will happen by 2029.
claim_summary: In an email published by Gary Marcus, Kurzweil says he has neither moved nor redefined his AGI prediction: AI doing any cognitive task an educated human can, by 2029.
timeline_text: I still still believe that will happen by 2029
definition_note: AGI = AI that can perform any cognitive task an educated human can; matching the best human poets is a higher bar that 'might take longer'
notes: also: definition. Kurzweil's email to Gary Marcus, printed verbatim in Marcus's Substack post 'Clarification from Ray Kurzweil' (22 June 2024); 'still still' is as printed. He explains that a remark to Steven Levy (Wired) meant only that writing at the level of the best poets might take longer than AGI. source_type blog because the statement is published on a blog; it is Kurzweil's own text.

quote: Human-level intelligence generally means AI that has reached the ability of the most skilled humans in a particular domain and by 2029 that will be achieved in most respects.
claim_summary: Kurzweil says AI will reach the ability of the most skilled humans in most respects by 2029, perhaps still trailing in a few skills.
timeline_text: by 2029 that will be achieved in most respects
definition_note: ability of the most skilled humans in a particular domain; 'in most respects' by 2029, may still lag top humans in a few skills such as Oscar-winning screenplays or deep new philosophical insights
notes: secondhand; PC Gamer story (8 July 2024, via Yahoo Tech) quoting the Guardian interview of 29 June 2024 (theguardian.com/technology/article/2024/jun/29/ray-kurzweil-google-ai-the-singularity-is-nearer), which the fetch tool could not reach. Hedge: 'in most respects'. Same story quotes 'We're going to expand intelligence a millionfold by 2045'.

quote: But that's now starting to look like a conservative view
claim_summary: Kurzweil says his 2029 date for AGI now starts to look conservative, implying it could come sooner.
timeline_text: now starting to look like a conservative view
definition_note: AGI matching or surpassing human capabilities across a wide range of cognitive tasks (the outlet's wording); same interview: the Singularity is 'where we no longer have control of AI'
notes: BBC Science Focus interview by Alex Hughes. Hedge toward an earlier date. The 2029 date is stated by the outlet in the sentence before the quote. Medium confidence because the definition is the outlet's.

quote: Basically, it will be able to do what an expert in every field can do, all at the same time, and we're not quite there yet, but we will be there by 2029.
claim_summary: Kurzweil defines AGI as doing what an expert in every field can do at once, says it is not here yet, and keeps 2029.
timeline_text: we're not quite there yet, but we will be there by 2029
definition_note: what an expert in every field can do, all at the same time
notes: also: capability_now, definition. TWiT Intelligent Machines episode 810 transcript (0:07:53). Asked whether he wants to adjust the date he said: 'Well, there's no reason for me to adjust it. I mean, I said 2029 in 1999.' (0:11:12). Same episode puts the Singularity, merging with AI, at 2045.

quote: In 1999, I predicted 2029 for AGI and I still predict 2029. Elon Musk says 2026. I think we'll have a lot of things that remind us of AGI, but we really won't be convinced in 2026. Maybe 2027, 2028. By 2029, I think everyone will accept it.
claim_summary: Kurzweil keeps 2029 for AGI, says 2026 will bring things that resemble AGI without convincing people, and expects universal acceptance by 2029.
timeline_text: we really won't be convinced in 2026. Maybe 2027, 2028. By 2029, I think everyone will accept it
definition_note: AGI; the article describes his bar as expert-level across thousands of fields
notes: secondhand; also: capability_now. Teamday.ai article summarising a Moonshots with Peter Diamandis podcast episode published 20 January 2026; the page says it is not a transcript. No transcript of the episode was found.

quote: As yet, we haven’t figured out how to build a machine that fully comprehends the concept of “dinner”, much less something as abstract as “harm” or “protection.” ... A.I. has a long way to go before laws as abstract as Asimov’s could realistically be encoded in software.
claim_summary: Today's AI cannot grasp even everyday concepts, so it is a long way from machines that could follow abstract ethical rules.
notes: also: post_agi; New Yorker online essay 'Moral Machines'. newyorker.com could not be reached, so the text was read from a PDF copy of the article on a Manchester University course page. Borderline: about machine understanding in general, not AGI by name.

quote: It's likely that machines will be smarter than us before the end of the century—not just at chess or trivia questions but at just about everything, from mathematics and engineering to science and medicine.
claim_summary: Machines will likely be smarter than people at almost everything before 2100, which is why their risks deserve thought.
timeline_text: likely ... before the end of the century
definition_note: smarter than us at just about everything (human-level or beyond, across all fields)
notes: secondhand; verbatim excerpt of Marcus's New Yorker blog post 'Why We Should Think About the Threat of Artificial Intelligence' (Oct 2013), quoted and linked on the Afflictor blog the next day. newyorker.com, web.archive.org and the ACM copy could not be read, so the original was not seen. also: post_agi. Cuts against his skeptic reputation: a 'likely' date in the 'whether' era.

quote: New York University professor Gary Marcus, CEO of Geometric Intelligence, says Hawking and Musk have a point, but the existential threat they fear is still many decades off and people face somewhat different threats from AI in the nearer term.
claim_summary: The threat from superintelligent machines that Hawking and Musk warn of is many decades away; nearer-term AI risks matter more.
timeline_text: still many decades off
definition_note: threat from superintelligent machines, not AGI as such
notes: secondhand; paraphrase of Marcus's Wall Street Journal essay 'Artificial Intelligence Isn't a Threat-Yet' (Dec 2014) as reproduced on David Luckham's blog. wsj.com could not be reached and follow-up searches (marcus-044 and marcus-112) found no other copy. Same page: Marcus says 'superintelligent' machines are unlikely to arrive soon.

quote: I don't think the robots are anywhere near as clever as Hal, and aren't going to be for at least thirty or fifty years or something like that.
claim_summary: Machines as clever as HAL, the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey, are at least 30 to 50 years away.
timeline_text: at least thirty or fifty years or something like that
definition_note: as clever as Hal (HAL 9000), i.e. human-level general AI
notes: computed: 2016 + 30 = 2046, 2016 + 50 = 2066; 'at least' makes both years lower bounds. Edge conversation (edited transcript of an interview).

quote: I still feel like we're actually no closer to the moon, where the moonshot is intelligence that's really as flexible as human beings. We're no closer to that moonshot than we were four years ago.
claim_summary: Deep learning has not brought AI any closer to intelligence as flexible as a person's.
definition_note: intelligence as flexible as human beings
notes: also: timeline (same interview: 'some people are hysterical about it, thinking that real AI is around the corner and it probably isn't'). Interview for the Flux podcast published as a transcript on TechCrunch.

quote: All-purpose, all-powerful AI systems, capable of catering to our every intellectual need, have been promised for six decades, but thus far still not arrived.
claim_summary: General-purpose AI has been promised for sixty years and is still not here; much remains to be solved.
definition_note: all-purpose AI catering to every intellectual need
notes: secondhand; MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy write-up of his November 2017 MIT seminar 'Artificial General Intelligence: Why Aren't We There Yet?', with direct quotes. Same write-up: 'We still have a long way to go for automated diagnosis, domestic robots, scene comprehension, and safe, reliable driverless cars.'

quote: I present ten concerns for deep learning, and suggest that deep learning must be supplemented by other techniques if we are to reach artificial general intelligence.
claim_summary: Deep learning on its own will not reach AGI; other techniques are needed.
notes: abstract of 'Deep Learning: A Critical Appraisal'. Treats AGI as reachable by a different route.

quote: But you know, we're pretty far from that right now. AlphaGo can play very well on a 19×19 board but actually has to be retrained to play on a rectangular board.
claim_summary: Current deep learning systems are far from general AI; they cannot transfer even simple skills.
notes: Answer to the question 'deep learning can't really reach general AI because it's missing deep understanding.' Interview about the book Rebooting AI. Same interview: 'A hundred years from now, AI will warrant our trust—and maybe sooner' (about trustworthiness, not AGI, so not coded as a timeline).

quote: In essence, GPT-2 has been a monumental experiment in Locke's hypothesis, and so far it has failed. Empiricism has been given every advantage in the world; thus far it hasn't worked.
claim_summary: GPT-2 shows that learning from huge data alone has not produced real understanding, contrary to talk of it as a step toward general intelligence.
notes: essay 'GPT-2 and the Nature of Intelligence' (The Gradient), rebutting the framing of GPT-2 as a step towards general intelligence. Borderline: about understanding rather than AGI by name.

quote: And it could be now we really are for the first time, 20 years away, where all these other times we weren't, or it could be we're still 50 years away.
claim_summary: Human-level AI might really be 20 years away this time, or still 50; nobody can tell.
timeline_text: 20 years away ... or it could be we're still 50 years away
definition_note: general AI with common sense
notes: computed: 2022 + 20 = 2042, 2022 + 50 = 2072. Sean Carroll's Mindscape podcast, episode 184 (published transcript). also: possibility (same episode: 'I just don't see any principled argument that says 500 years from now, people will still be smarter than machines, I just don't see it.').

quote: I seriously doubt it. In truth, we are still a long way from machines that can genuinely understand human language, and nowhere near the ordinary day-to-day intelligence of Rosey the Robot
claim_summary: Deep learning will not do everything; machines are still far from understanding language or everyday intelligence.
definition_note: ordinary day-to-day intelligence (Rosey the Robot)
notes: magazine essay 'Deep Learning Is Hitting a Wall'; replying to Hinton's 2020 claim that deep learning 'is going to be able to do everything'.

quote: Being realistic, 7 years might well not be enough to (a) invent those tools (if they are don't already exist) and (b) take them from the lab into production.
claim_summary: Seven years, to 2029, is probably too short to reach AGI; he offers Musk a bet that AI will not pass at least three of five tests in 2029.
timeline_text: 7 years might well not be enough
definition_note: bet test: in 2029 one AI passing at least three of five tasks (understand a movie, understand a novel, cook in an unfamiliar kitchen, write 10,000 lines of bug-free code from a spec, formalize proofs)
notes: computed: 2022 + 7 = 2029. Reply to Elon Musk's prediction of AGI by 2029; the post sets out the bet ('I offered to place a bet on it'). timeline_year is the year he doubts, not an expected date.

quote: We are still likely decades away from general-purpose, human-level AI that can understand the true meanings of articles and videos or deal with unexpected obstacles and interruptions.
claim_summary: General-purpose, human-level AI is probably still decades away.
timeline_text: still likely decades away
definition_note: general-purpose, human-level AI that understands meaning and copes with the unexpected
notes: Scientific American essay 'Artificial General Intelligence Is Not as Imminent as You Might Think'. also: possibility (same essay: 'Machines may someday be as smart as people and perhaps even smarter, but the game is far from over.')

quote: My own skepticism has limits. I do think we will eventually reach AGI (artificial general intelligence), and quite possibly before the end of this century.
claim_summary: AGI will eventually be built, quite possibly before 2100.
timeline_text: quite possibly before the end of this century
notes: also: possibility; dialogue with Grady Booch, who argued AGI will not come in our lifetimes. Later in the dialogue Marcus asks 'Why be so sure we can't do that in the next 75 years?' Cuts against his skeptic reputation.

quote: I still don't think large language models have much to do with superintelligence or artificial general intelligence [AGI]
claim_summary: Large language models have little to do with AGI or superintelligence; fast self-improvement is not an immediate possibility.
notes: also: self_improvement, timeline (same post: worries of others 'seem to center mainly around what happens if computers rapidly and radically self-improve themselves, which I don't see as an immediate possibility'; and 'I don't know when we will get to such machines').

quote: When we get to artificial general intelligence, maybe let's say it's 50 years, that really is gonna have, I think, profound effects on, on labor.
claim_summary: Told the US Senate that AGI might be about 50 years away and will have profound effects on jobs when it comes.
timeline_text: maybe let's say it's 50 years
notes: incidental; also: timeline; computed: 2023 + 50; found by the Altman trace (altman-033), quote re-checked against the transcript by the coordinator; stance could be read as cautious

quote: Sooner or later, we will get to artificial general intelligence and we should be figuring out what we're going to do when we get there. I'm not here to say I see a great solution to all of this. These are serious problems, I'm worried about them.
claim_summary: AGI will come sooner or later, and he is worried we are not ready for it.
timeline_text: Sooner or later
notes: also: post_agi, timeline; conversation with Yascha Mounk (Persuasion, published transcript). Same conversation: 'I don't think anybody knows where we'll be in 20 years'. Cuts against his skeptic reputation.

quote: Let's not dumb down our standards, and wind up with a bunch of machines we can't rely on, just so that big tech can prematurely declare victory, when there is plenty of work left to do.
claim_summary: AGI is not imminent; current machines fall short and claims of near AGI lower the bar.
definition_note: argues Shane Legg's 2023 bar (beating typical human performance on cognitive tasks) is weaker than earlier definitions
notes: also: timeline, definition (post title: 'No, Virginia, AGI is not imminent'). Reply to Shane Legg.

quote: But there is zero justification for claiming that the current technology has achieved general intelligence.
claim_summary: Large language models are not AGI, despite claims that AGI is already here.
definition_note: My bar for AGI is a machine that can do the cognitive tasks that people can typically do.
notes: Reply to Blaise Agüera y Arcas and Peter Norvig, 'Artificial General Intelligence Is Already Here'.

quote: Skeptical of this, I offered Musk a $1 million bet that AGI superior to the smartest individual humans would not arrive by the end of 2025
claim_summary: AGI smarter than the smartest people will not arrive by the end of 2025; he offered Musk a $1 million bet on it.
timeline_text: would not arrive by the end of 2025

notes: timeline_year is the year by which he says it will not arrive. Same bet as his 2024-04-09 open letter ('$10 million says we won't see human-superior AGI by the end of 2025'), treated as one occasion.

quote: If you read his manuscript, please read it for his concerns about our underpreparedness, not for his sensationalist timelines.
claim_summary: Rejects the forecast of AGI by 2027 as sensational but says we are badly unprepared for AGI whenever it comes.
timeline_text: AGI whenever it comes
notes: also: post_agi; reply to Leopold Aschenbrenner's AGI-by-2027 forecast. Same post: 'woefully underprepared for AGI whenever it comes'.

quote: Both of us agree that the achievement of 8 out of 10 of these tasks would be strong evidence for the G (General) in Artificial General Intelligence having been achieved.
claim_summary: Bet with Miles Brundage on whether AI can do 8 of 10 hard tasks by the end of 2027; Marcus takes the side that it will not.
timeline_text: by the end of 2027
definition_note: 8 of 10 listed cognitive tasks
notes: Co-written with Miles Brundage in the third person. Stakes: $2,000 from Marcus against $20,000 from Brundage; the post tells readers not to infer Gary's beliefs from the odds, so no probability is recorded.

quote: We will not see artificial general intelligence this year, despite claims by Elon Musk to the contrary.
claim_summary: AGI will not arrive in 2025.
timeline_text: will not see artificial general intelligence this year
notes: timeline_year is the year by which he says it will not arrive.

quote: AGI isn't coming in 2025, and GPT-5 probably isn't either.
claim_summary: AGI will not arrive in 2025.
timeline_text: AGI isn't coming in 2025
notes: timeline_year is the year by which he says it will not arrive. Same post: 'I will stand by my own predictions that we won't see AGI in 2025'.

quote: Gary Marcus stands by his prediction that we will not see AGI in 2025, and regrets that Elon Musk didn't take his million dollar bet.
claim_summary: Repeats that AGI will not arrive in 2025.
timeline_text: will not see AGI in 2025
notes: Written in the third person on his own newsletter. Reply to Sam Altman's 'We are now confident we know how to build AGI'. timeline_year is the year by which he says it will not arrive.

quote: And even though I highly doubt AGI will arrive in three years, I can't absolutely promise you it won't happen in 10.

notes: also: self_improvement (criticizes the AI 2027 scenario's superhuman AI researcher); computed: 2025 + 3 = 2028 (doubted), 2025 + 10 = 2035 (not ruled out); year left blank because he bounds both sides rather than naming an expected date. Same post: the scenario 'almost certainly underestimates how much time we have to prepare for general intelligence, by years if not decades'. Cuts against his reputation.

quote: "The chances of A.G.I.'s arrival by 2027," notes Marcus, "now seem remote."
claim_summary: AGI by 2027 now looks very unlikely.
timeline_text: The chances of A.G.I.'s arrival by 2027 ... now seem remote
notes: secondhand; quoted from his New York Times guest essay 'The Fever Dream of Imminent Superintelligence Is Finally Breaking' (2025-09-03, nytimes.com/2025/09/03/opinion/ai-gpt5-rethinking.html) on the Simanaitis Says blog; nytimes.com could not be reached and his newsletter post of the same day only links to the essay. timeline_year is the year by which he doubts it.

quote: But contrary to the impression you get from that piece, it turns out Gary Marcus thinks AGI is coming in 10-25 years. Ish, he hastens to add.
claim_summary: AGI is coming in roughly 10 to 25 years, possibly sooner; four years is very unlikely.

notes: secondhand; Daniel Reeves's newsletter (2025-09-12) reporting Marcus's view, apparently from conversation, with no link to a Marcus source; same paragraph: 'when pressed, he admits that less than 10 years is also possible. He calls 4 years "awfully unlikely".' computed: 2025 + 10 = 2035, 2025 + 25 = 2050. Follow-up search (marcus-122) found no primary source. Cuts against his skeptic reputation.

quote: I am someone who believes that AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) could change the world, but also someone who thinks that LLMs are not the right path there, morally or technically.
claim_summary: AGI could change the world, but large language models are not the way to it.

notes: also: possibility, definition; post introduces his New York Times op-ed of the same day and a multi-author paper defining AGI.

quote: LLMs have their place, but anyone expecting the current paradigm to be close to AGI is delusional.
claim_summary: Today's large language models are not close to AGI.
notes: also: timeline (post title: 'Game over. AGI is not imminent, and LLMs are not the royal road to getting there.')

quote: We won't get to AGI in 2026 (or 7).
claim_summary: AGI will not arrive in 2026 or 2027.
timeline_text: We won't get to AGI in 2026 (or 7)
notes: timeline_year is the last year by which he says it will not arrive.

quote: Current AI systems are powerful and increasingly useful tools, but they do not exhibit the flexible, self-directed competence that the original concept of artificial general intelligence was intended to capture.
claim_summary: Today's AI is useful but is not AGI, despite claims that AGI has already arrived.
definition_note: original sense: robust, flexible competence across a wide range of environments and tasks
notes: also: definition; post 'Rumors of AGI's arrival have been greatly exaggerated', arguing that some have weakened the definition of AGI.

quote: The view of this substack since its inception has been that scaling would not lead to AGI — and it hasn't.
claim_summary: Making models bigger has not produced AGI.
notes: 'its inception' is a link in the original; link markup removed. Post reacts to Sam Altman saying major breakthroughs beyond scaling are needed.

quote: Marcus lays out the additional breakthroughs he believes will be required for AGI, including better world model construction, temporal and spatial reasoning, and the ability to induce structured representations from raw data – challenges he believes will take at least a decade to solve.
claim_summary: The breakthroughs AGI needs will take at least a decade.
timeline_text: at least a decade
notes: secondhand; organizer's summary of his on-stage conversation with Will Wilson at Bug Bash 2026; no transcript found (follow-up marcus-120). computed: 2026 + 10 = 2036, a lower bound.

quote: Getting to AGI will require new ideas, not just new code optimizations.
claim_summary: AI improving its own code will not by itself produce AGI, which is harder than self-improvement.
notes: Reply to an Anthropic blog post on recursive self-improvement (an AI 'capable of fully autonomously designing and developing its own successor'); a heading in the post says AGI is harder than recursive self-improvement.

quote: we will not get to AGI in 2026. happy to put money on that, @jason, if you dare.
claim_summary: AGI will not arrive in 2026; he offers to bet on it.
timeline_text: we will not get to AGI in 2026
notes: post on X; text and date read through the api.fxtwitter.com mirror of the post. timeline_year is the year by which he says it will not arrive.

quote: The idea that we have reached that point is laughable.
claim_summary: Rejects Sam Altman's and Elon Musk's claims that we are already in the Singularity.
definition_note: Singularity: the point where our ability to foresee events collapses, a step beyond AGI
notes: post 'Sorry, Sam and Elon, we have not reached the Singularity'; 'that point' is the Singularity as defined in the preceding sentences. Dismissive of the claim, not of the long-run possibility.

quote: By conventional definitions, Astra still falls short.
claim_summary: Rejects Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's claim that AGI has arrived; the newest model, Astra, is not AGI.
definition_note: conventional definitions
notes: Same post: 'When real AGI arrives, we won't need to squint our eyes.'

quote: The bad news is that Premise 1 (sorry I can't handle the British spelling) is almost certainly true, though I seriously doubt it will happen by 2030.
claim_summary: Superintelligence is almost certainly coming eventually, but very unlikely by 2030.
timeline_text: seriously doubt it will happen by 2030
definition_note: superintelligence (Premise 1 of a doom argument; its exact wording is in an image that could not be read)
notes: also: post_agi; next sentence: 'we all think that the field needs more breakthroughs before we reach superintelligence'. Saying it is almost certainly coming cuts against his skeptic reputation. timeline_year is the year by which he doubts it.

quote: We will achieve rat-level intelligence before we achieve human-level, so let's work on rat-leve intelligence
claim_summary: In slides titled 'Towards Human Level AI' for a NIPS 2005 workshop, LeCun treats human-level AI as an achievable goal reached through learning, but says we are still far from even rat-level intelligence, which must come first.
definition_note: human-level AI, reached via rat-level first; agents must build themselves through learning
